chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the wiping upon the two feet, how it is (to be done). So he placed his palm upon the toes and wiped them up to the two ankles, up to the back of the foot. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supposing if a man were to do it with two fingers from his fingers, like this?' So he said: 'No, except with his palm'.
ai.seo_question: How should one wipe the feet during ablution according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) serves as a foundational proof for the Shia position of wiping the top of the feet (masah al-rajulayn) rather than washing them, a key distinction from the Sunni schools. The Imam’s physical demonstration clarifies the specific anatomical boundaries—from the toes to the ankles—and explicitly invalidates the practice of wiping with only two fingers, emphasizing the necessity of using the entire palm. This narration underscores the importance of adhering to the precise method prescribed by the Ahl al-Bayt in ritual purity.
